# ZeRO-3: copy offloaded master weights back to the device through pinned buffers

<!-- r3 2026-10-15: branch peng-fix-zero3-offload-pinned-copy-v2 (worktree
/fsx/peng/workspace/ds-fix-zero3-offload-pinned-copy) on master 5f266e26d; the change is the same as v1's (local
branch peng-fix-zero3-offload-pinned-copy-v1 on dcd8595c2, never pushed). Master moved 2 commits, neither in
stage3.py or the test file. FINAL DRAFT v2, 2026-10-13, for a new PR (no PR exists yet). Patch:
pr-prep/patches/2026-10-13/zero3-offload-pinned-copy-v2.patch on master dcd8595c2 (worktree
pr-prep/r2/zero3-offload-pinned-copy, not committed). v1 of this draft: zero3-offload-pinned-copy-body.md (test in
tests/unit/runtime/zero/, which PR CI does not select). Job IDs of every result: SOURCES.md. The submitter fills the last section. -->

**Part of:** #8672 (Q4 2026 roadmap), "Enable training of large scale models".

## Summary

With `offload_optimizer.device: cpu`, ZeRO-3 copies each sub-group's updated float32 master partition back to the
device from host memory that is never pinned, even with `pin_memory: true` (the default since #8207). This PR copies
it through two fixed-size pinned buffers instead, with the same values.

- Qwen2.5-32B, 8 H200, whole optimizer on the CPU: 11.96 s to 10.35 s per step (-13.5%), same peak memory.
- MiniMax-M3 (all 60 layers, 4 nodes x 8 H200, 65% of the optimizer on the CPU): 126.9 s to 123.9 s per step.
- Extra host memory: a fixed 256 MiB of pinned memory per rank (bf16).

## Duplicate check

Searched issues and PRs on 2026-10-13 ("offload pinned fp32 partition", "zero3 offload pin_memory copy",
"fp32_partitioned_groups_flat", "offload ratio pinned", "pageable offload"). Related, not duplicates: #8207 (merged:
pinned the ZeRO-3 gradient offload buffers, default `pin_memory: true`; master partitions unchanged), #8256 (merged:
routes pin sites through `get_accelerator().pin_memory()`; this PR uses the same accelerator calls), #8618 (closed:
a CPU-offload benchmark).

Sibling path: ZeRO-1/2 does not have the defect. It pins the float32 partition and casts into a pinned bf16 buffer
of the partition's size before a `non_blocking` copy (`stage_1_and_2.py` lines 546-558 and 2841-2844).

## Root cause

`_create_fp32_partitions` (`stage3.py`) builds each CPU master partition with `.to('cpu', dtype=...)` and
`.clone().detach()`, which is pageable memory whatever `pin_memory` says. After the CPU optimizer step,
`_reassign_or_swap_out_partitioned_parameters` runs `fp16_flat.data.copy_(fp32_flat.data)`: a blocking copy from CPU
float32 to device bf16. For a blocking copy with a dtype change, PyTorch converts on the CPU into a new pageable bf16
tensor of the whole partition, copies it from pageable memory and synchronizes.

Found in a profile (MiniMax-M3, first 8 layers, 8 H200, 75% of the optimizer on the CPU, rank 0): 13 bare
`aten::copy_` host-to-device copies of 576 MiB per step from pageable memory, at 3-7 GB/s, 1,648 ms per step.

## The change (`deepspeed/runtime/zero/stage3.py`, 49 added, 2 removed lines)

| Where | What |
|---|---|
| `_reassign_or_swap_out_partitioned_parameters` | uses the new copy when `offload_optimizer.pin_memory` is true, the source is on the CPU and not pinned (`get_accelerator().is_pinned`), and the destination is on the device; every other case keeps `dst.copy_(src)` |
| new `_copy_through_pinned_staging(dst, src)` | two pinned buffers of 2**26 elements in `dst`'s dtype (`get_accelerator().pin_empty`, created on first use). Per piece: wait for the previous copy out of this buffer (an event), cast the piece into the buffer on the CPU, `copy_(..., non_blocking=True)` to the device, record an event. Before returning, wait for the last piece |
| `__init__`, `_unpin_offload_buffers` | the buffer size and state; release of the buffers (matters under `DS_PIN_MEMORY_BACKEND=native`) |

Design notes:
- **Why not pin the master partitions, as ZeRO-1/2 does:** a `non_blocking` copy from pinned float32 into a bf16
  tensor converts on the device and needs a float32 device temporary of the sub-group's size. Avoiding that needs a
  pinned bf16 buffer of each partition's size, as ZeRO-1/2 keeps. Either way pinned host memory would grow with the
  model, and PyTorch's pinned allocator rounds each allocation up to a power of two. The two buffers here have a fixed
  size; 2**26 is a power of two, so nothing is rounded up.
- **Same values:** the CPU cast is the one the blocking copy did before (round to nearest even), so the device
  partition is bitwise the same.
- **Stream order:** the pieces are copied on the current stream, and an event guards each buffer's reuse. The final
  wait keeps what callers had before: the partition is on the device when the function returns. The next forward's
  parameter all-gathers run on their own stream, and it does not wait for the main stream.
- **Host synchronization:** at most one piece-sized wait per buffer reuse and one at the end. The old path blocked
  for the whole copy.

## Measured

Qwen2.5-32B (all 64 layers, real weights), 1 node of 8 H200 (143,771 MiB, driver 580.126.09), torch 2.8.0+cu126.
Settings:
- ZeRO-3 with `offload_optimizer: {device: cpu, pin_memory: true}`;
- float32 master weights and Adam states, DeepSpeedCPUAdam with 12 threads per rank;
- bf16, one 8,192-token PG-19 sequence per GPU, activation checkpointing, lr 1e-6;
- mean of steps 3-8; one run per row.

| | master `dcd8595c2` | this PR |
|---|---|---|
| step time | 11.96 s | **10.35 s** |
| step time with `wall_clock_breakdown` | 11.72 s | 10.01 s |
| rank 0: forward / backward | 1.21 / 3.73 s | 1.21 / 3.72 s |
| rank 0: `step` / of which the sub-group loop (`optimizer_step`) | 5.98 / 5.73 s | 5.03 / 3.64 s |
| peak device memory (rank 0) | 34.66 GB | 34.66 GB |
| loss at steps 1 / 2 / 8 | 0.022649 / 0.976567 / 1.746324 | 0.022649 / 0.976611 / 1.746344 |

The losses differ from step 2 by run-to-run variation. Two master runs differ by as much: step 2 is 0.976376 with
`wall_clock_breakdown` and 0.976567 without it. The flash-attention backward adds with atomics. The bitwise check is
the unit test below.

<details><summary>MiniMax-M3 runs (DeepSpeed master + unmerged MiniMax-M3 model code: #8658, #8652)</summary>

Settings for both: ZeRO-3 + AutoEP (expert parallel 8), real weights, each 65,536-token sequence split over 4 GPUs,
65% of the optimizer on the CPU (`offload_optimizer.ratio` 0.65), float32 master + Adam.

- 4 nodes x 8 H200, all 60 layers, same nodes, back to back: 126.9 s without, 123.9 s with
  (mean of steps 3-10); peak device memory 132.4 GB in both.
- 1 node, first 8 layers: 14.09 s without, 12.46 s with; losses equal at every printed step.

</details>

This change, and the fused CPU Adam change stacked on it, were in the DeepSpeed tree of our MiniMax-M3 and GLM-5.2
runs against Megatron-LM (real weights, 65,536-token sequences, 80-95% of the optimizer on the CPU):

| Model | Nodes | DeepSpeed, s/step | Megatron-LM, s/step | How measured |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| MiniMax-M3, all 60 layers | 4 x 8 H200 | 85.24 | 119.35 | one job, same nodes, mean of steps 4-23 |
| GLM-5.2, first 38 layers | 4 x 8 H200 | 62.03 | 63.73 | one job, same nodes, mean of steps 4-23 |
| GLM-5.2, all 78 layers | 8 x 8 H200 | 130.58 | 135.56 | separate jobs on 7 of the same 8 nodes, mean of steps 6-10 |

On one node (first 4 layers of each model), master plus this PR, the fused CPU Adam PR and the two model
PRs (#8658, #8659) gives the same loss at every step as that tree.

## Tests

New: `TestZero3OffloadPinnedCopyBack` in `tests/unit/v1/zero/test_zero.py` (2 ranks, `ratio` 1.0 and 0.5,
`sub_group_size` 20,000 so partial offload has sub-groups on both sides).
- It trains 3 steps with `pin_memory: false` (direct copy) and with `pin_memory: true`, and requires the gathered
  parameters to be bitwise equal.
- It also requires that only the pinned run used the staging buffers. Otherwise the test would compare the direct
  copy with itself.
- The piece size is set to 1,000 elements, so each step refills both buffers many times.

The test is in `tests/unit/v1` so that PR CI selects it. With this diff, the `modal-torch-latest` selector
(`ci/tests_fetcher.py`) picks 85 test files, including `tests/unit/v1/zero/test_zero.py`. I simulated the selector's
diff with the working-tree files, since nothing was committed.

Commands, from `tests/`, on 1 node of 8 H200 (143,771 MiB, driver 580.126.09), torch 2.8.0+cu126, pytest 9.1.1:

```
# master + only the new test: 2 failed, AttributeError: no attribute '_staging_buffers'
# master + this PR:
pytest unit/v1/zero/test_zero.py -k TestZero3OffloadPinnedCopyBack        # 2 passed
pytest unit/v1/zero/test_zero.py unit/v1/zero/test_zero_user_backward.py unit/v1/pin_memory/ \
    -k "offload or Offload or pin or Pin"                                  # 61 passed, 1 skipped (torch_npu)
pytest unit/v1/zero/test_offload_states.py                                 # 128 passed
pytest unit/runtime/zero/test_zero_offloadpp.py unit/v1/pin_memory/        # 50 passed
# on master 5f266e26d (2026-10-15, this change plus the fused CPU Adam PR stacked on it):
pytest unit/v1/zero/test_zero.py::TestZero3OffloadPinnedCopyBack            # 2 passed
pytest unit/runtime/zero/test_zero_offloadpp.py                             # 3 passed (master: 3 passed)
```

The last two ran on the first version of this patch, whose `stage3.py` differs from this one only in two comments;
the timings above also used the first version.

## Compatibility

| Cell | Validated |
|---|---|
| ZeRO-3, CPU optimizer offload, `pin_memory` true, whole optimizer on the CPU | yes: new test (ratio 1.0); Qwen2.5-32B |
| ZeRO-3, partial offload (`ratio` < 1) | yes: new test (ratio 0.5); MiniMax-M3 on 1 and 4 nodes |
| ZeRO-3, `pin_memory` false | unchanged path; the new test's reference |
| bf16 | yes. fp16: not run (same path; the cast is the same CPU cast) |
| ZeRO-3, NVMe optimizer offload | not run. Expected unchanged: the swapped-in buffers are pinned, so the direct copy is kept |
| ZeRO-3 + ZenFlow, `DS_PIN_MEMORY_BACKEND=native` | not run |
| ZeRO-1/2 | not affected |
| Accelerators other than CUDA | not run; only `get_accelerator()` calls are used (`pin_empty`, `is_pinned`, `Event`, `unpin_memory`) |

No config, checkpoint or public API change.

## AI assistance

This change, its tests and this description were prepared with AI assistance (Claude).

files.patch:
@@ -251,6 +251,11 @@ def __init__(
 
         self.offload_optimizer = False
         self.offload_optimizer_pin_memory = False
+        # Pinned buffers for copying CPU master partitions back to the device (_copy_through_pinned_staging). The
+        # element count is a power of two, so the pinned allocator does not round the buffers up.
+        self._staging_numel = 2**26
+        self._staging_buffers = None
+        self._staging_events = None
         self.offload_optimizer_fast_init = False
         self.offload_param = False
         self.offload_param_pin_memory = False
@@ -562,6 +567,8 @@ def _unpin_offload_buffers(self):
                 accelerator.unpin_memory(buffer)
         for buffer in getattr(self, 'hp_params_pin_buffers', []):
             accelerator.unpin_memory(buffer)
+        for buffer in getattr(self, '_staging_buffers', None) or []:
+            accelerator.unpin_memory(buffer)
         unpin_offloaded_optimizer_states(self.optimizer)
         if self.offload_optimizer_pin_memory:
             for fp32_partition in self.fp32_partitioned_groups_flat:
@@ -2849,13 +2856,53 @@ def _post_step(self, timer_names):
         see_memory_usage('After zero_optimizer step', force=False)
         print_rank_0("------------------Finishing Step-----------------------")
 
+    @instrument_w_nvtx
+    def _copy_through_pinned_staging(self, dst, src):
+        """Copy the pageable CPU master partition ``src`` into the device partition ``dst`` through two small pinned
+        buffers: each piece is cast on the CPU into one buffer while the previous piece is copied from the other.
+
+        Copies from pageable memory run at a few GB/s. Pinning the master partitions themselves, as ZeRO-1/2 does,
+        would also need a pinned low-precision buffer of each partition's size, so pinned host memory would grow with
+        the model; these two buffers have a fixed size."""
+        numel = src.numel()
+        chunk = self._staging_numel
+        if self._staging_buffers is None or self._staging_buffers[0].dtype != dst.dtype:
+            self._staging_buffers = [get_accelerator().pin_empty(chunk, dtype=dst.dtype) for _ in range(2)]
+            self._staging_events = [None, None]
+        src = src.view(-1)
+        dst = dst.view(-1)
+        last_event = None
+        for index, start in enumerate(range(0, numel, chunk)):
+            buf = index % 2
+            if self._staging_events[buf] is not None:
+                # The previous copy out of this buffer must finish before the buffer is refilled.
+                self._staging_events[buf].synchronize()
+            count = min(chunk, numel - start)
+            staging = self._staging_buffers[buf][:count]
+            staging.copy_(src[start:start + count])
+            dst[start:start + count].copy_(staging, non_blocking=True)
+            event = get_accelerator().Event()
+            event.record()
+            self._staging_events[buf] = event
+            last_event = event
+        # Callers expect the partition on the device when this returns: the parameter all-gathers of the next forward
+        # run on a stream that does not wait for this one.
+        if last_event is not None:
+            last_event.synchronize()
+
     @instrument_w_nvtx
     def _reassign_or_swap_out_partitioned_parameters(self, sub_group_id):
         if self.fp16_partitioned_groups_flat[sub_group_id] is not None:
             # When torch autocast is enabled, groups in fp16_partitioned_groups are in fp32 already and those in
             # fp32_partitioned_groups are aliases. Calling tensor.data.copy_ will not trigger any copy in that case.
-            self.fp16_partitioned_groups_flat[sub_group_id].data.copy_(
-                self.fp32_partitioned_groups_flat[sub_group_id].data)
+            dst = self.fp16_partitioned_groups_flat[sub_group_id].data
+            src = self.fp32_partitioned_groups_flat[sub_group_id].data
+            accelerator = get_accelerator()
+            src_is_pageable = src.device.type == "cpu" and not accelerator.is_pinned(src)
+            if self.offload_optimizer_pin_memory and src_is_pageable and dst.device.type != "cpu":
+                self._copy_through_pinned_staging(dst, src)
+            else:
+                dst.copy_(src)
 
             #unflatten fp16 parameter subgroup
             self._unflatten_partitioned_parameters(sub_group_id)

@@ -1919,6 +1919,70 @@ def test(self, force_ds_optim):
             model, _, _, _ = deepspeed.initialize(model=model, optimizer=optimizer, config=config_dict)
 
 
+@pytest.mark.skipif(not get_accelerator().is_bf16_supported(), reason="bf16 is not supported on this accelerator")
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("ratio", [1.0, 0.5])
+class TestZero3OffloadPinnedCopyBack(DistributedTest):
+    """With pin_memory, the updated CPU master partitions must reach the device with the same values as the direct
+    copy from pageable memory (pin_memory False): the parameters after training are compared bitwise. The pinned run
+    must actually go through the staging buffers, or the test would compare the direct copy with itself."""
+    world_size = 2
+
+    def _train(self, pin_memory, ratio):
+        hidden_dim = 256
+        config_dict = {
+            "train_micro_batch_size_per_gpu": 2,
+            "optimizer": {
+                "type": "Adam",
+                "params": {
+                    "lr": 1e-3
+                }
+            },
+            "bf16": {
+                "enabled": True
+            },
+            "zero_optimization": {
+                "stage": 3,
+                "sub_group_size": 20000,
+                "offload_optimizer": {
+                    "device": "cpu",
+                    "pin_memory": pin_memory,
+                    "ratio": ratio
+                }
+            },
+        }
+        torch.manual_seed(0)
+        model = SimpleModel(hidden_dim, nlayers=4)
+        model, _, _, _ = deepspeed.initialize(model=model, model_parameters=model.parameters(), config=config_dict)
+        # Pieces much smaller than a sub-group, so the copy refills both staging buffers many times per step: a buffer
+        # refilled before its previous copy finished would change the values.
+        model.optimizer._staging_numel = 1000
+        torch.manual_seed(1)
+        data_loader = random_dataloader(model=model,
+                                        total_samples=6,
+                                        hidden_dim=hidden_dim,
+                                        device=model.device,
+                                        dtype=torch.bfloat16)
+        for batch in data_loader:
+            loss = model(batch[0], batch[1])
+            model.backward(loss)
+            model.step()
+        params = []
+        for p in model.module.parameters():
+            with deepspeed.zero.GatheredParameters([p]):
+                params.append(p.detach().clone().cpu())
+        used_staging = model.optimizer._staging_buffers is not None
+        return params, used_staging
+
+    def test(self, ratio):
+        direct, direct_used_staging = self._train(pin_memory=False, ratio=ratio)
+        staged, staged_used_staging = self._train(pin_memory=True, ratio=ratio)
+        assert not direct_used_staging
+        assert staged_used_staging
+        assert len(direct) == len(staged)
+        for a, b in zip(direct, staged):
+            assert torch.equal(a, b)
+
+
 @pytest.mark.parametrize("training", [True, False])
 class TestZeroPartitionCache(DistributedTest):
     world_size = 1
